title: Asymmetric Michael reaction for the synthesis of chiral  trans -dialkyl nitroalkanals, key building blocks for natural products – a review
content: The Michael addition provides a powerful means of carbon–carbon bond formation, and in the presence of a chiral catalyst, affords vicinal trans-dialkyl stereocenters. The reaction conditions are extremely mild. With a nitroalkene and an alkanal, the resulting nitro and formyl functional groups in the 4-nitro-1-alkanal provide versatile sites for selective functionalization. While the Michael addition was first reported in 1887, the asymmetric Michael reaction emerged in the early 2000s. In this review, all known (190) examples of the asymmetric Michael reaction with a nitroalkene and an alkanal are reported. Particular foci are the four types of chiral catalysts, the reaction conditions, the methods of assessing stereochemical integrity, and the diverse nitroalkanal products. The resulting trans-2,3-dialkyl-4-nitro-1-alkanals have been used to gain access to complex natural products.
